firstPlayerRule: The player who most recently watched a horror movie leads the first trick of the first round.
clarifications: The winner of each trick leads the next trick.
A later round starts with the player who gained the lowest score in the preceding round. If that score is tied, the rules let the players decide the starter by any appropriate method.

internalEvidence: Publisher-hosted English PDF was retrieved and both pages rendered and visually inspected. Local source: research/source-files/fudacoma-artipia/10-tricks-later-en.pdf; SHA-256 02e1fd345d8a1e1fda2a16edc66d73e34a67d0644c51a7b641e682750ab4d892. Setup step 5 assigns the first Lead Player to the person who last watched a horror movie; later trick and round leaders use different instructions. Codex editorial review under the owner's 2026-09-22 authorization: publisher PDF was reopened on 2026-09-24; setup step 5 and Card Play on page 1, and next-trick and next-round leader rules on page 2, confirm the exact answer. The first-round criterion is eligible for the random mix because it independently selects an opening player without components. The flexible tie method belongs only to subsequent rounds.
uncertainty: The first-round horror-movie criterion has no stated tie-break.
The answer applies to the identified English publisher file; other editions may differ.
